cues.en: All right. First of all, thank you everybody for showing up today, especially at 9 o'clock on a Saturday morning. I appreciate it. Would I want to talk to you? Could you give us a foreground? What I want to talk about today is a new concept I call dynamic binary visualization. And I think this is a pretty important and interesting topic, because I really do this as the future of first engineering, which I think is a pretty bold statement. But I'll let you be the judge of whether or not that's accurate at the end of the presentation.
cues.zh: 好的。首先，非常感谢大家今天能来，尤其还是周六早上 9 点，真的太感谢了。我今天要讲什么呢？可以帮我们调一下前面的声音吗？我今天想聊的是一个我称之为“动态二进制可视化”的新概念。我认为这是一个非常重要且有趣的话题，因为我确实将其视作逆向工程的未来——我知道这说法挺大胆的。但到底准不准，演讲结束时留给大家来评判。

cues.en: So before we get into things, I've got to go through the obligatory bioslides, and these are kind of dry and boring, so I'll try to speed through this. Basically, my name is Chris Domis. I'm an embedded systems engineer in the cyber innovation unit in the national security division of the Battelle Memorial Institute now. A lot of people haven't heard of Battelle, but we are the world's largest nonprofit R&D organization, and we manage some of the leading national laboratories around the world. So I'm not here to be a show for my company, but we do a lot of cool work. Hopefully, some of that you'll see today.
cues.zh: 在正式开始前，我得先过一下例行的个人简介幻灯片，这些内容有点枯燥，我会尽量快点讲完。简单来说，我叫 Chris Domis。我现在是 Battelle Memorial Institute 国家安全部门网络创新部门的嵌入式系统工程师。很多人可能没听说过 Battelle，但我们是全球最大的非营利研发机构，管理着全球多所顶尖的国家实验室。我不是来给公司打广告的，但我们确实做了很多很酷的工作，希望今天能向大家展示其中一部分。

cues.en: So I've been writing two things. What I want to talk to you about is reverse engineering and specifically our view of reverse engineering as a type of information analysis. And in other words, we get a big binary blob or a big binary data stream and we need to decide what is this and what does this do. So when we view reverse engineering through this lens, I think there's two ever-present issues that we need to be able to address.
cues.zh: 言归正传，我想和大家探讨的是逆向工程，具体来说，是将逆向工程视作一种信息分析的视角。换句话说，当我们拿到一个庞大的二进制数据块或数据流时，需要判断它是什么、能做什么。当我们从这个视角审视逆向工程时，我认为有两个始终存在的问题需要解决。

cues.en: The first is how we conceptualize binary information. The second is how we use our conceptualization for analysis. And I think there are big flaws with the way we approach both of these issues. And that's sort of what I want to tackle today. So let's look at the first problem, how we conceptualize binary information. So it brings us to what I consider to be an RE dichotomy. There's two polar opposite approaches here, and they're basically mutually exclusive, where on the left we have our conventional approach, which is essentially a hexa-dump of information. It gives us a raw binary information. It's very flexible because this doesn't tell us what the information is.
cues.zh: 第一，我们如何概念化二进制信息；第二，我们如何利用这种概念化来进行分析。我认为目前解决这两个问题的方法都存在很大缺陷，这也正是我今天想要探讨的。我们先来看第一个问题：如何概念化二进制信息。这就引出了我认为的逆向工程“二分法”。这里有两种截然相反、基本互斥的方式：左边是传统方法，本质上就是信息的十六进制转储。它展示的是原始二进制信息，非常灵活，因为它不会直接断定信息具体是什么。

cues.en: is, it leaves that analysis up to us. It's also a very exact representation of the data. There's no question that what I'm seeing is what the data really is. Unfortunately, it's unreasonably complex and it's very difficult to deal with information this way.
cues.zh: 它把分析的工作完全留给了我们。这同样是对数据极其精准的呈现，毫无疑问，我们看到的即是数据的真实面貌。但遗憾的是，它的复杂度极其离谱，用这种方式处理信息往往异常艰难。

cues.en: So most people tend to go to the alternate approach, something like a disassembly. It tends to be something very rigid and it's governed by rules and structure, but it has been a bit of being very succinct and it's very easy for us to comprehend this. So it's not so much that I have a problem with either of these two approaches of conceptualizing binary information. The real problem is that there's a giant chasm between these two and it's completely empty. There's really no software, no conceptualization approaches that bridge this gap here. And that's one of the issues I want to address.
cues.zh: 大多数人往往会选择另一种方法，比如反汇编。它通常非常死板，受规则和结构约束，但也相当简洁，很容易理解。所以，并不是说我对这两种概念化二进制信息的方法有意见。真正的问题在于，这两者之间存在一道巨大的鸿沟，而且完全是空白的。目前确实没有软件、也没有概念化方法能弥合这个鸿沟。而这就是我想解决的问题之一。

cues.en: And if we look at the second problem, how we use that conceptualization of binary information for an analysis of binary data, here what we're looking at is essentially the questions of what does this do or where's the vulnerability, questions reverse engineers are usually interested in. And I know guys who can look at a function graph and instantly tell you what that function is doing without even reading the disassembly, just by the way the nodes are connected. Alternatively, I know guys who can just leap through hundreds of pages of disassembly and instantly find the vulnerabilities there. And it's a pretty amazing ability.
cues.zh: 如果我们看第二个问题，即如何利用这种二进制信息概念化来分析二进制数据，本质上关注的是“这是做什么的”或者“漏洞在哪里”，这些逆向工程师通常关心的问题。我认识一些人，他们看一眼函数图，甚至不用读反汇编，仅凭节点连接方式就能立刻告诉你这个函数在做什么。反过来，我也认识一些人，他们能快速翻过数百页反汇编，立刻找到其中的漏洞。这能力相当惊人。

cues.en: But what I find is these guys usually have a lot of trouble telling you how they came to their conclusions. And I think the reason for that is that in this current state, reverse engineering is very much an art. And I think there's a problem with that because we're far enough along. We've been doing this for long enough. We should have better approaches for this.
cues.zh: 但我发现，这些人通常很难说清楚自己是怎么得出结论的。我认为原因在于，在目前的状态下，逆向工程很大程度上是一门艺术。我觉得这有问题，因为我们已经发展得足够远了，做这件事也够久了，应该有更好的方法。

cues.en: I want to fix those problems. I want to bridge the gap in our analysis tools, find some happy medium between hex dumps in our high-level analysis tools like Ida Pro. And I also want to change RE from an art to a science. So those are ambitious goals. So how can we accomplish those things? Well, I think we have the tools available through two things. The first is going to be what I call visual reverse engineering. This is going to address the issue of binary conceptualization, how we understand binary data. The second way we can tackle these problems is through statistical exploration techniques.
cues.zh: 我想解决这些问题。我想弥合分析工具中的鸿沟，在十六进制转储和像 Ida Pro 这样的高级分析工具之间找到某种折中。我还想把逆向工程从一门艺术变成一门科学。这些都是很有野心的目标。那我们要怎么实现呢？我认为可以借助两样东西。第一种是我所说的可视化逆向工程。它将解决二进制概念化的问题，也就是我们如何理解二进制数据。第二种应对这些问题的方法，是统计探索技术。

cues.en: And this is going to address the issue of how we analyze binary information.
cues.zh: 这将解决我们如何分析二进制信息的问题。

cues.en: The statistical side of things gets a little dry unless you're really into math, and it really goes into too much depth that I don't have time to cover today. So we're going to mostly skip over this. I'll show you some of the ways we can use statistics, but I'm not going to go into the algorithms in too much depth. What I really want to focus on is the visual reset of things, which I think is really the more interesting approach for most people. So let's dive into that and see what I mean by visual reverse engineering. So the idea here is that we can take a computationally difficult task and translate it into a problem that our brains do very well for.
cues.zh: 统计这一侧会有点枯燥，除非你真的很喜欢数学，而且它会深入太多细节，我今天没时间覆盖。所以我们基本会跳过这部分。我会展示一些使用统计的方法，但不会深入讲算法。我真正想重点讲的是可视化这一侧，我认为对大多数人来说，这其实是更有意思的方法。那么让我们深入看看，我说的可视化逆向工程是什么意思。这里的想法是，我们可以把一个计算上困难的任务，转化成我们大脑非常擅长处理的问题。

cues.en: we're going to take the difficult task of understanding binary information and translate that to something we're very good at. In this case, that is understanding visual information. So our visual cortexes are very powerful. We are really good at processing 3D and spatial information. So if we can find a way to translate binary information to visual representations, we can analyze it much faster than normally possible.
cues.zh: 我们要把理解二进制信息这项艰巨的任务，转化为我们非常擅长的事情。在这里，也就是理解视觉信息。我们的大脑视觉皮层非常强大，特别擅长处理 3D 和空间信息。因此，如果我们能找到一种方法把二进制信息转化为视觉呈现，就能以远超以往的速度去分析它。

cues.en: So in other words, I'm going to find a way to traverse 100,000 pages of binary garbage in a very short amount of time. And we're going to understand exactly what was in there, just as if we had been looking at the hexadecimal itself. The fundamental idea here is that if we fundamentally change the way we process binary information, we can find unexpected ways of making sense of it.
cues.zh: 换句话说，我要找一种方法，在极短的时间内快速扫过十万页二进制垃圾数据。而且我们能精确理解里面的内容，就像直接看十六进制代码一样。这里的核心思路在于，如果我们从根本上改变处理二进制信息的方式，就能以出人意料的途径去理解它。

cues.en: So that's really what I'm trying to accomplish. And if you've never spent 30 hours looking at a hex dump wondering what the heck is this stuff, you might be wondering why bother. Aren't our current analysis tools powerful enough that they already do what we need? And the answer is they're absolutely not. And there are a lot of reasons for that, but I want to focus on two big points. So the biggest issue I see is that our best reverse engineering tools are completely dependent on a known structure.
cues.zh: 这就是我真正想要实现的目标。如果你从未花上 30 个小时盯着十六进制转储抓狂，你可能会纳闷何必费这个劲。难道现有的分析工具还不够强大、不能满足我们的需求吗？答案是：绝对不够。原因有很多，但我想重点谈两点。我认为最大的问题在于，我们最好的逆向工程工具完全依赖于已知的结构。

cues.en: The problem with that is that information is evolving faster than our tools can keep up with it. So every day there's a new instruction set. There's a new data format, a new file format, some new format that we need to be able to support. And our tools have to constantly play catch up in order to be able to analyze this type of information. And it's a losing game. This stuff's just exploding at a rate that we can't keep up with. So being tied to structure in this way is hugely problematic. We need to find a better way of analyzing information that's completely independent of structure if we want to be able to keep up with things.
cues.zh: 问题在于，信息演进的速度已经超过了工具跟进的速度。每天都会有新的指令集、新的数据格式、新的文件格式，各种我们需要支持的新格式层出不穷。而我们的工具必须不断疲于奔命，才能勉强分析这类信息。但这是一场注定会输的追逐战，新东西正以我们无法企及的速度爆发式增长。因此，像这样受制于结构存在巨大的弊端。如果我们想跟上时代，就必须找到一种完全独立于结构的信息分析方式。

cues.en: The other issue might be colloquially called Gates' Law, named after that guy that we all love. So this essentially says that software is getting slower, more rapidly, and hardware becomes faster. It's basically the counter to Moore's Law. And what this means from a reverse engineering perspective is that the amount of information we need to analyze is growing exponentially. So if processor power is doubling every 18 months, the number of instructions that that processor is actually executing is growing at an even faster rate. So from a reverse engineering perspective, that means we have a lot more information to analyze.
cues.zh: 另一个问题俗称 Gates' Law（盖茨定律）——以我们都熟知的那位大佬命名。它的大意是：软件变慢的速度，比硬件变快的速度还要快。它基本上是摩尔定律的反面。从逆向工程的角度来看，这意味着我们需要分析的信息量正在呈指数级增长。如果处理器算力每 18 个月翻一番，那么它实际执行的指令数量增长得甚至还要更快。所以在逆向工程看来，这意味着我们要分析的信息呈爆炸式增长。

cues.en: And we just can't keep up because our tools aren't becoming exponentially more powerful. There aren't a whole lot of new reverse engineers able to tackle these problems. And we're not getting any better at collaborating on reverse engineering problems, which means this is another losing game. We're never going to be able to keep up with things at the pace we're currently going.
cues.zh: 我们根本跟不上，因为我们的工具并没有呈指数级变得更强大。也没有大量新的逆向工程师能来解决这些问题。而且我们在逆向工程的协同上也毫无起色，这意味着这又是场必败之局。照目前的节奏，我们永远都不可能跟得上。

cues.en: So I think this is a really big problem in first engineering and if you haven't run across this already You can see this more and more in the future So this needs to be addressed and I was sort of shocked to find when I started investigating this that there are only really two people
cues.zh: 所以我认为这是逆向工程领域的一个大问题，如果你现在还没遇到，未来也会越来越频繁地碰上。因此这亟待解决，而当我开始调研时震惊地发现，实际上只有两个人

cues.en: who has done any sort of real research into this field. Two guys named Greg Conte and Aldo Partese, both brilliant guys, and I want to talk a little bit about some of their work into this field and talk about how we can extend what they've done. So Conte, I'll talk about first. He's a smart guy. He teaches at the United States Military Academy. And at 2010 at Black Hat, he gave a presentation that still today is the best Black Hat presentation I've ever seen. So I'll talk a little bit about what he talked about there. And for Pete, the other guy I want to look at, he runs a small software company called NullCube.
cues.zh: 在这个领域做过真正的研究。这两位叫 Greg Conte 和 Aldo Partese，都是非常厉害的人，我想聊聊他们在这个领域的一些工作，以及我们该如何拓展他们的成果。首先谈谈 Conte。他很聪明，任教于美国西点军校。他在 2010 年 Black Hat 上的演讲，至今仍是我看过的最佳 Black Hat 演讲。我会稍微聊聊他当时分享的内容。至于另一位我想介绍的人，他经营着一家名为 NullCube 的小型软件公司，

cues.en: runs a blog called courte.c. So if you're interested in malware or reverse engineering, there's a great blog to read, and I'll introduce some of his ideas as well. But let's look at Conti first. Conti posited that even in unstructured data, there is some type of structure. And barring any other information about what type of information we're looking at, we can assume that sequential bytes have some kind of implicit relationship. So Conti's only dilemma is
cues.zh: 还写一个叫 courte.c 的博客。如果你对恶意软件或逆向工程感兴趣，那是非常值得一读的博客，我也会介绍他的一些想法。不过我们先看 Conti。Conti 提出，即便在非结构化数据中，也存在某种结构。在对所分析的信息类型一无所知的情况下，我们可以假定连续字节之间存在某种隐式关联。所以 Conti 唯一的难题就是：

cues.en: How do we conceptualize and understand our relationship if we have no idea what it is? And so here's where Conti's genius comes into play. He came up with a very simple approach for visualizing the relationship between sequential bytes and data. He said, what we're going to do is take sequential bytes and a string of information and translate those to xy coordinates. So in this case, if we have a string like dirty time,
cues.zh: 如果我们完全不知道这种关联是什么，该如何去概念化并理解它？这就是 Conti 的天才之处发挥作用的地方了。他想出了一种非常简单的方法，来可视化数据中连续字节之间的关系。他说，我们要做的就是把一串数据中的连续字节提取出来，转换成 xy 坐标。比如在这里，如果我们有一个像 dirty time 这样的字符串，

cues.en: where it's going to take all the switchabytes in the string and transit those to x, y. So d is ascii, hex 64, e is ascii, hex 65, that becomes 64, 65, and x, y coordinates. And we're just going to plot those in a Cartesian system here. And when we do that, what we start to see is from marker.
cues.zh: 就会把字符串里的所有连续字节提取并转换为 x、y。比如 d 的 ASCII 码是十六进制 64，e 是十六进制 65，这就变成了 xy 坐标中的 (64, 65)。然后我们把它们绘制在笛卡尔坐标系中。当我们这样做时，开始看到的景象极其……

cues.en: remarkable patterns for any type of information we're trying to look at. So here's what Conti's found when you look at ASCII information. So even though this algorithm had no concept of what type of structure was within ASCII information, we see clear structure and patterns in the visual representation through this algorithm. So what we're actually seeing here are these different artifacts that are each caused by some type of structure or some type of relationship in the ASCII data. So this is caused by lowercase letters followed by lowercase letters. This is uppercase followed by uppercase uppercase by lowercase, lowercase by
cues.zh: 无论分析何种类型的信息，都能呈现出惊人的规律。这就是 Conti 在观察 ASCII 信息时的发现。即便这个算法完全不了解 ASCII 信息内部存在怎样的结构，我们也能通过它在可视化呈现中看到清晰的结构和模式。我们在图中实际看到的这些不同图样，都是由 ASCII 数据中的某种结构或关联所引起的。比如这是小写字母紧跟小写字母产生的，这是大写接大写，大写接小写，小写接……

cues.en: and these various lines are caused by slash-r, slash-n spaces. So all those implicit relationships, the way that data is intrinsically laid out within ASCII data results in structure that we can see here. And you found that regardless of what type of information you're looking at, there's clear structure. So here he's looking at image data, here he's looking at audio data.
cues.zh: 而这些不同的线条则是由 \r、\n 和空格产生的。因此所有这些隐式关系，即数据在 ASCII 内部固有的排列方式，就构成了我们在此看到的结构。而且他发现，无论观察什么类型的信息，都有清晰的结构。比如这里他观察的是图像数据，这里看的是音频数据。

cues.en: And the benefit here is I can almost instantly learn to recognize these images for what they are, whereas trying to analyze that information at a hexadecimal level would take a tremendous amount of time.
cues.zh: 好处是，我几乎能立刻学会识别这些图像代表什么，而在十六进制层面分析信息会耗费大量时间。

cues.en: So I think this was a big step forward in improving the way that we conceptualize binary information. But that's really just the tip of the iceberg, and that's where we started our investigation. But before I get into that, let me look at some of the stuff a guy named Cortezy did. So now, unfortunately, I had to chop most of Cortezy's slides for the sake of brevity. But he found a way to use a fractal called the Hilbert curve to improve the way we conceptualize binary information. Essentially, what he found is that if we map data to this curve first before presenting it to the user,
cues.zh: 所以我认为，这是改进我们理解二进制信息方式的一大步。但这只是冰山一角，我们的研究也正是从这里开始。不过在深入之前，先看看一个叫 Cortezy 的人做过的一些东西。遗憾的是，为了简洁，我不得不删掉 Cortezy 的大部分幻灯片。但他找到了一种方法，用一种叫希尔伯特曲线的分形来改进我们对二进制信息的理解。本质上，他发现如果先把数据映射到这条曲线，再呈现给用户，

cues.en: We have this important aspect that we preserve locality which assists our brains in interpreting information. So without going into the details of that.
cues.zh: 我们就有一个重要特性：保留局部性，这有助于大脑解读信息。具体细节就不展开了。

cues.en: Here he's mapped it into a Hilbert curve, and here he's laid things out in a more intuitive fashion, line by line. But what this shows us is that we can get more detailed information from the Hilbert translation when we look at it this way. So tiny little artifacts like this little red block here indicate unique features inside of this data set that I can't see without mapping it to the Hilbert curve first. So we make extensive use of this Hilbert curve in our software. And I'll leave it up to you to visit Cortez's site if you're interested more information about how that can be used.
cues.zh: 这里他把它映射到希尔伯特曲线，这里他又按行以更直观的方式排布。但这说明，当我们这样看时，可以从希尔伯特转换中得到更详细的信息。所以像这里小红块这样的细小痕迹，表示数据集中有独特特征，而如果不先映射到希尔伯特曲线，我就看不到这些特征。因此我们在软件中大量使用希尔伯特曲线。如果你有兴趣了解更多用法，可以去 Cortez 的网站看看。

cues.en: But that basically brings us to software reaping and developing. I thought these guys had some really great ideas. Conti and Portezi are two brilliant people, but I felt like they didn't bring their ideas to their fullest potential. They didn't pursue things as far as they really could have gone. So I wanted to take it further than they ever did. So Conti has some software called BenVase that you can get at his website. And I tried to use that for binary analysis, but it just wasn't robust enough. It couldn't give me enough information.
cues.zh: 这基本上就把我们带到了软件逆向与开发。我觉得这些人有一些很棒的想法。Conti 和 Portezi 都是非常聪明的人，但我觉得他们没有把想法发挥到最大潜力。他们没有推进到真正能达到的程度。所以我想比他们走得更远。Conti 有个叫 BenVase 的软件，可以在他的网站上获取。我试着用它做二进制分析，但它不够健壮，无法给我足够的信息。

cues.en: to do any sort of meaningful analysis on binary data. So I wanted to go further in that. cues.zh: 这些算是别人提出的一些思路。当然，我们对其进行了扩展，让它们更具交互性，更适用于实际分析。但现在我想讲讲我们自己提出的想法。我们发现的一个更强大的方法是二进制分类。我在这里想实现的目标，本质上就是刚才看到的：遍历整个文件，根据这些模式识别不同区域。但我希望通过统计分析来实现这一过程的自动化。而这正是我们通过这些分类算法做到的。我们的做法是提取一些二进制数据，

cues.en: that represents a sample of something I'm looking for. So for example, if I want to find x86, I can compile x86 out of some other file and supply that as a template to my software. So the key here is I'm just saying this is what x86 looks like. I'm not completely defining x86.
cues.zh: 作为我想寻找的目标样本。比如，如果我想找出 x86 代码，可以从其他文件编译出 x86 并作为模板提供给软件。关键在于，我只是在告诉它 x86 长什么样，并没有给出 x86 的完整定义。

cues.en: I'm not giving it a grammar. I'm not telling it how to parse x86. I'm just giving it a sample of x86 code. And I'm going to give it a whole bunch of these different templates. And from these templates, our software builds what are called n-gram models. And we do a statistical algorithm called naive-based classification algorithm in order to classify regions of the file as most closely matching various templates. So now I can feed any arbitrary file into our software. And it will run it against these templates in order to identify the different regions. So here it's saying, well, this region most closely matches from its
cues.zh: 我没有给它语法规则，也没教它怎么解析 x86，只是给了它一段 x86 代码样本。我会提供一大堆这样不同的模板。软件会根据这些模板构建所谓的 n-gram 模型。然后我们采用一种称为朴素贝叶斯分类的统计算法，将文件的各个区域归类为与各种模板最匹配的类型。这样一来，我可以把任意文件输入到软件中，它会拿去与这些模板比对以识别出不同的区域。所以在这里它会说，从其

cues.en: statistical pattern perspective, this most closely matches your x86 template. This most closely matches your compressed template. This looks like ASCII here. So it's a neat, automated way to do file carving, but it has uses far beyond that.
cues.zh: 统计模式的角度来看，这个区域最符合你的 x86 模板，这个区域最符合你的压缩数据模板，而这里看起来像是 ASCII。所以这是一种巧妙且自动化的文件雕刻（file carving）方式，但它的用途远不止于此。

cues.en: So one of the things we'll see coming up is using this to identify custom and proprietary formats. But with these statistical matching techniques, we can automate that process as long as I can find a small snippet of instructions from this piece of malware, or whatever I'm looking for, I can supply that as a template, and then find that throughout the rest of the file based on the patterns present in that data. cues.zh: 完全都是 x86。但我想在那个文件里找加密算法。加密算法的字节和指令分布、模式会和普通 x86 不一样。所以我可以输入一个 x86 加密算法，然后说：找更多像这样的东西。它就能解析出来。它能够解析一个文件，并寻找在统计上匹配的内容。它能够说：这个文件里还有这些其他加密算法。所以我认为这是个非常强大的想法，能帮我们在逆向工程中节省大量时间。

We're actually able to identify call graphs inside of an arbitrary binary file through statistical patterns rather than grammar definitions. So what we're looking at here is essentially a call graph for a file that I gave that was parsed using statistics.
cues.zh: 问题在于，我不想让我们的软件依赖任何特定类型的结构。我不想那样被绑定到 x86 或 ARM 上。所以我不想把如何解析这些东西的知识写死进去。我仍然希望能获得解析带来的好处。于是我们想出了所谓的概率解析。我们实际上能够通过统计模式，而不是文法定义，在任意二进制文件里识别调用图。所以这里我们看到的基本上就是我给出的一个文件的调用图，它是用统计方法解析出来的。

cues.zh: 而不是直接进行反汇编。这赋予了我们极强的信息分析能力，无论是 x86、ARM，还是明天刚出、谁都没见过的全新指令集，我都能运行完全相同的算法，并且依然能生成这些函数图，稍后我会展示这到底有多好用。

And just a little bit of background, EFI is basically a BIOS replacement. It's supposed to be more structured, more extensible, and more secure. And one of the things you can do with EFI is you can
cues.zh: ……几年前的 Black Hat 上做过一场演讲，叫“攻击 Intel BIOS”。这个思路非常绝，我也正想用这些分析技术来深入研究它。他们这篇论文的目标是绕过 EFI 签名保护。顺便交代一点背景，EFI 基本上就是 BIOS 的替代品。它理应结构更完善、扩展性更强、也更安全。通过 EFI 你可以做到的一件事是……

cues.en: One of the ways it's more secure is it can be configured so that it requires signed images if you want to re-flash your BIOS or EFI. That way you can't get unexpected code sold on the firmware of your system because it has to be signed. So if that's supposed to make it more secure, but these guys had invisible things, we wanted to get around that.
cues.zh: 它更安全的一个表现是，可以配置为在重刷 BIOS 或 EFI 时必须使用带签名的镜像。这样未经允许的代码就无法写入系统固件，因为它必须有签名。按理说这能大幅提升安全性，但 Invisible Things 的这帮人却想绕过它。

cues.en: So what they did is they started investigating EFI images, and they found that the image itself is not signed. The image is only an envelope with a CRC checksum, but inside of that envelope are signed modules. So they found signed module after signed module after signed module, and then they came across an unsigned module, which was a perfect attack vector. We can flash this unsigned module without having to sign it, which gives us a way into the system.
cues.zh: 于是他们开始研究 EFI 镜像，发现镜像本身并没有签名。镜像只是一个带 CRC 校验和的外壳，但外壳里面是一个个签名模块。他们找到一个又一个签名模块，接着突然发现了一个未签名模块，这简直是绝佳的攻击向量。我们无需签名就能刷入这个未签名模块，从而拿到了攻入系统的途径。

cues.en: Why would you do that? Why would you require signing on these things to improve security and then give the opportunity for an unsigned module? Well, the reason for this is the unsigned module is the boot splash logo. So when you first press the power button on your PC, the image that comes up is a splash screen that's an unsigned module in this EFI system. And the reason they leave that unsigned is because they want OEMs to be able to add their own splash screen to the system without having to go through the trouble of signing things. So that's an interesting...
cues.zh: 为什么要这么做呢？既然为了提升安全性要求模块必须签名，又为什么留出一个未签名模块的机会？原因是，这个未签名模块其实是开机画面 Logo。当你按下电脑电源键时，首先跳出来的那个开机画面，在 EFI 系统里就是一个未签名模块。之所以不签名，是为了让 OEM 厂商能轻松换上自己的开机画面，而不用大费周章地走签名流程。这挺有意思的……

cues.en: possibility for an exploit here, and they found a way to leverage this to their advantage. Their goal was to get unsigned code execution. cues.zh: 这里存在利用漏洞的可能，他们也找到了加以利用的方法。他们的目标是实现未签名代码执行。他们想运行自己的代码来替代 BIOS，从而尽早控制系统，但他们无法直接更新代码。代码必须有签名，而他们唯一能更新的只有位图。

cues.en: But what they did is they found a vulnerability in the bitmap parser for the splash screen. So most EFI code comes from this EFI template code provided by Intel and then IBCs or independent bios vendors use that code for their EFI development. So finding a vulnerability in this template code means that you're finding a vulnerability in every EFI system out there.
cues.zh: 但他们做的是在开机画面的位图解析器中找到了一个漏洞。大部分 EFI 代码都源自 Intel 提供的 EFI 模板代码，然后 IBV（独立 BIOS 供应商）再用这些代码来进行 EFI 开发。所以在这个模板代码里找到漏洞，就意味着在市面上所有的 EFI 系统中都找到了漏洞。

cues.en: So they found that they could flash the bitmap with an invalid image by manipulating the width and height to get an overflow when this image is parsed. And through that overflow, they can get code execution early on in the BIOS boot process. So that's a pretty powerful ability. And I wanted to look at that in more depth. Well, one observation we need to make before we go forward is that no one is really EFI. And Invisible Things sort of glosses over the spec to make it look like this is a fairly straightforward hack, but it's not at all because BIOS vendors have a lot of legacy code.
cues.zh: 他们发现可以通过篡改宽高来刷入一张无效的位图，使图像解析时发生溢出。通过这个溢出，他们就能在 BIOS 启动过程的早期执行代码。这是一种非常强大的能力。我想对此做更深入的研究。在继续之前，我们需要注意一点：其实没有谁是纯粹的 EFI。Invisible Things 在规范上有点一笔带过，让这看起来像是一个相当直接的利用，但其实完全不是，因为 BIOS 供应商有大量的遗留代码。

cues.en: and they're gradually moving towards EFI, but they're not really willing to give up their legacy code yet. So what you find are systems that are 25% EFI and 75% legacy bios or something like that. What that means from our perspective is that we can still use this vulnerability.
cues.zh: 他们正逐步转向 EFI，但还不太愿意放弃遗留代码。所以你会看到大概 25% 是 EFI、75% 是传统 BIOS 这样的系统。从我们的角度来看，这意味着我们仍然可以利用这个漏洞。

cues.en: But we're dealing with much less structure than EFI would provide, because we're dealing with more bios, and bios is very unstructured.
